name: Kava USDX
who_can_redeem: Kava Mint borrowers repay USDX to close or reduce collateralized debt positions and reclaim eligible collateral.
redemption_region_notes: Access depends on Kava network, supported collateral, wallet, application, governance parameters, liquidity, and applicable restrictions.
redemption_notes: USDX is not a fiat issuer claim. Its primary protocol exit is repayment and burn against Kava Mint debt, while market conversion depends on available liquidity.
summary: Kava-native U.S.-dollar stablecoin minted through overcollateralized Kava Mint debt positions, publicly launched with BNB collateral and still documented as an active Kava protocol asset.
notes: Growth B / Batch R. Full collateral, parameter, module-version, supply, and market-liquidity history remain explicit open items.

name: Bean
who_can_redeem: Bean does not represent a direct fiat redemption claim. Holders use market liquidity and Beanstalk protocol functions; protocol debt positions are settled according to Field and Barn mechanics.
redemption_region_notes: Access depends on Arbitrum, supported interfaces, protocol state, governance, market liquidity, wallet support, and applicable restrictions.
redemption_notes: Bean targets one U.S. dollar through decentralized credit, supply, demand, liquidity, and governance incentives rather than conventional reserve redemption.
summary: Beanstalk protocol stablecoin first deployed in August 2021, paused after the April 2022 governance exploit, replanted in August 2022, and later migrated from Ethereum to Arbitrum while remaining an active protocol identity.
notes: Growth B / Batch R. Old Ethereum Bean tokens are obsolete; current Arbitrum identity, recapitalization state, governance control, and full contract lineage remain separately recorded.
